campaigns.title: tuned_guest_metal
campaigns.question: Is the tuned guest (1 vCPU / 1 GiB, no omnibox preload, a quiet console, huge pages) cheaper per task on a metal host than on c8i.xlarge?
campaigns.answer: No: on m8i.metal-48xl (192 vCPUs) the tuned guest held at least 200 browsers, the harness's cap, and one burst cost ≈ $0.164 per 1,000 tasks against ≈ $0.044 for one on c8i.xlarge (tuned_guest_host_size). With 4 KiB pages it held 192, one burst ≈ $0.183; host CPU ran out at 200.

campaigns.title: tuned_guest_host_size
campaigns.question: Is the tuned guest (1 vCPU / 1 GiB, no omnibox preload, a quiet console, huge pages) cheaper per task on a 4-vCPU or a 16-vCPU c8i host?
campaigns.answer: The 4-vCPU host is cheaper: c8i.xlarge cost ≈ $0.043 per 1,000 tasks, c8i.4xlarge (16 vCPUs) ≈ $0.046 and m8i.4xlarge not tuned ≈ $0.133. Host CPU ran out first on all three.

campaigns.title: guest_boot_tuning
campaigns.question: Do a quiet guest console and huge pages cut CPU per task on headless Chromium without its omnibox preload?
campaigns.answer: Yes, huge pages most: on c8i.xlarge the default guest cost ≈ $0.090 per 1,000 tasks, quiet console ≈ $0.082, huge pages ≈ $0.067, both ≈ $0.060 and 1 vCPU / 1 GiB tuned ≈ $0.042. On m8i.4xlarge huge pages cut ≈ $0.132 to ≈ $0.079; host CPU ran out first.

campaigns.title: tuned_guest_warm_start
campaigns.question: With a 5 s warm start, is the tuned guest (1 vCPU / 1 GiB, no omnibox preload, a quiet console, huge pages) cheaper per task than a 2 vCPU / 2 GiB microVM?
campaigns.answer: Yes: warm, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB tuned cost ≈ $0.043 per 1,000 tasks against ≈ $0.106 for 2 vCPU / 2 GiB and ≈ $0.079 for plain 1 vCPU / 1 GiB. Host CPU ran out first; cold, the tuned guest cost the same (guest_boot_tuning).

campaigns.title: metal_chromium_no_preload
campaigns.question: Does headless Chromium without its omnibox preload fit more microVMs on a metal host?
campaigns.answer: Yes: without the preload one m8i.metal-48xl (192 vCPUs) held at least 200 browsers, the harness's cap, against 140 with it (metal_host_tight_slo). One burst cost ≈ $0.186 per 1,000 tasks instead of ≈ $0.219.

campaigns.title: chromium_no_preload
campaigns.question: Does turning off headless Chromium's hidden omnibox preload lower CPU per task?
campaigns.answer: Yes: without the preload c8i.xlarge cost ≈ $0.099 per 1,000 tasks instead of ≈ $0.108, and m8i.4xlarge ≈ $0.133 instead of ≈ $0.146. Host CPU ran out first everywhere.

campaigns.title: microvm_size_cold
campaigns.question: Does a 1-vCPU microVM cost less per task than a 2-vCPU one?
campaigns.answer: No, not started cold: on c8i.xlarge, 2 vCPU / 2 GiB cost ≈ $0.107 per 1,000 tasks; 1 vCPU / 2 GiB held 1 browser, one burst costing ≈ $0.217. With 1 vCPU the host was never full: each browser's own vCPU was busy starting up.

campaigns.title: microvm_size_warm
campaigns.question: Does a warm start lower the cost per task, once its wait is charged?
campaigns.answer: No: warm, 2 vCPU / 2 GiB cost ≈ $0.114 per 1,000 tasks against ≈ $0.107 cold (microvm_size_cold). Warm, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB was cheapest at ≈ $0.101 and 1 vCPU / 2 GiB ≈ $0.103, each holding 4 browsers on c8i.xlarge; host CPU ran out first.

campaigns.title: small_c8i_hosts
campaigns.question: Does a smaller c8i host cost less per 1,000 tasks?
campaigns.answer: Yes, at every step down: c8i.xlarge cost ≈ $0.108 per 1,000 tasks, c8i.2xlarge ≈ $0.118, c8i.4xlarge ≈ $0.124 and m8i.4xlarge ≈ $0.146. Host CPU ran out first on every host.

campaigns.title: metal_host_tight_slo
campaigns.question: At the nested campaigns' step targets (p50 within 1 s, p95 within 2 s), how many microVMs fit on a metal host?
campaigns.answer: One m8i.metal-48xl (192 vCPUs) held 140 browsers at ≈ $0.123 per 1,000 tasks, against 9 at ≈ $0.150 on a nested m8i.4xlarge (16 vCPUs, m8i_host_size). Host CPU ran out first at 144.

campaigns.title: metal_host
campaigns.question: How does a metal host change density per vCPU and cost?
campaigns.answer: One m8i.metal-48xl (192 vCPUs) held at least 192 browsers, every count passing; the harness caps a host at 200. One burst cost ≈ $0.219 per 1,000 tasks, judged at the design's step targets, task p95 within 5 s and ready within 900 s.

campaigns.title: host_memory
campaigns.question: With 4 GiB microVMs, does half the host memory lower density?
campaigns.answer: No: with 4 GiB browsers, c8i.4xlarge (32 GiB) held 9 at ≈ $0.139 per 1,000 tasks and m8i.4xlarge (64 GiB) held 8 at ≈ $0.150. Host CPU ran out first on both, never memory.

campaigns.title: hypervisor
campaigns.question: Does Cloud Hypervisor fit as many microVMs as Firecracker?
campaigns.answer: Yes: Cloud Hypervisor held 9 browsers on m8i.4xlarge (16 vCPUs) at ≈ $0.145 per 1,000 tasks, Firecracker 9 at ≈ $0.146, Firecracker with MMIO 8 at ≈ $0.144. Host CPU ran out first every time.

campaigns.title: m8i_host_size
campaigns.question: Is density per host vCPU the same on 8 and 16 vCPU hosts?
campaigns.answer: Close: m8i.4xlarge (16 vCPUs) held 9 browsers at ≈ $0.150 per 1,000 tasks, m8i.2xlarge (8 vCPUs) held 4 at ≈ $0.132. Host CPU ran out first on both.

campaigns.title: baseline
campaigns.question: How many microVMs fit on one m8i.4xlarge?
campaigns.answer: One m8i.4xlarge (16 vCPUs) held 8 browsers of 2 vCPU / 2 GiB, ≈ $0.141 per 1,000 tasks. Host CPU ran out first at 12; 9–11 were not tried.
